 Kings provide medical update on Keegan Murray, Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell
 Sacramento will have to ride out this road trip without much in terms of reinforcements. Plus, the Kings exercise Nique Clifford's third-year option. 
 By Blake | 16 Comments | Oct 26, 2026 
 Dec 21, 2025; Sacramento, California, USA; Sacramento Kings forward Keegan Murray (13) and center Dylan Cardwell (32) and center Maxime Raynaud (42) and guard Nique Clifford (5) prepare to light the beam in celebration of their win against the Houston Rockets at Golden 1 Center. Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images
 The Sacramento Kings are going to have to wait a bit longer for reinforcements. The team sent a medical update out Monday regarding the status of Keegan Murray, Maxime Raynaud and Dylan Cardwell.
 Raynaud is out at least another two weeks from a right patellar subluxation. Murray is out another 10-14 days because of the ankle. Cardwell is out another week at least with a left calf strain.
 The full report is below:
 “Sacramento Kings center Maxime Raynaud is progressing well in his rehabilitation following a right patellar subluxation sustained during the game against the Golden State Warriors on Oct. 10. He will be listed as out and will be reevaluated in approximately two weeks. Kings center Dylan Cardwell continues his return-to-play process following a left calf strain and will begin on-court activities. Cardwell will be listed as out and will be reevaluated in approximately seven days. Kings forward Keegan Murray experienced soreness and stiffness in his left ankle following the Kings game against Portland on Oct. 23. Murray has been diagnosed with left ankle capsulitis and will be listed as out. He will be reevaluated in approximately 10 to 14 days.”
 The front court and defense in general could use these guys right now. Sacramento kicks off a four-game road trip Tuesday against the San Antonio Spurs.
 In other news, the Kings have exercised the third year option on Nique Clifford . This comes as he seems to have fallen out of Doug Christie’s rotation in the last few games.
